_comment: Source of truth for /proof/. Every entry comes from a record under docs/release/ (or docs/perf/); never add a pass the record does not show. records.title: Release 1.1.0 lab regression sweep
records.environment: Linux runner (Ubuntu 24.04 amd64, VM, 8 cores) with podman 4.9.3, kind 0.30, OpenSSL 3.5.4 and cosign 3.1.3. Compose, SSE and HA legs on an Apple silicon Mac with podman 6.1.3.
records.what_ran: The 1.0.0 tests/live harness sweep, repeated on the 1.1.0 tag, plus the smoke suite.
not_proven: Windows domain harnesses (GPO autoenroll, WSTEP matrix, WinRM discovery, IIS, RDP and SQL install, agent MSI) were not run in this pass.
macOS keychain, vendor SCEP appliances, F5 and NetScaler, and real cloud key stores were not run.
make lint, go test and the UI suites were not part of this pass.
The storm profile misses its own zero-violation gate; the successor run on the key-usage branch had one acme failure and one pass.
records.note: Three harnesses did not pass. pqc-wave failed on the runner because Go 1.26 cannot complete a TLS handshake with an ML-DSA certificate; it passed on the Mac and the build moved to Go 1.27. inventory-sources failed from test rot (the Entrust fixture). The storm profile finalizes 2000 of 2000 in both legs with no duplicates but breaks its strict limit gate. Two areas failed: inventory sources (test fixture out of date) and the renewal storm limit gate (8 and 18 rate-limit violations, 375 s against a 360 s goal). Neither was a regression from 1.0.0.

records.title: ML-DSA delivery to Apache, and Kubernetes Secret rollback
records.environment: Apple silicon Mac, podman 6.1.3, kind 0.33. Apache httpd 2.4.69 with mod_ssl on OpenSSL 3.5.9 (Alpine; systemd and apachectl replaced by shims). A kind workload on OpenSSL 3.5.9 reading a TLS Secret.
records.what_ran: A three-member wave. One Apache host took an ML-DSA-65 certificate over SSH. A second Apache host and the Kubernetes Secret were forced to fail verification and had to roll back to the old certificate.
not_proven: A verify failure caused by a real product fault, such as a workload that cannot parse an ML-DSA key.
Apache from Debian or RHEL packages, mod_md, or a proxy in front of httpd.
ingress-nginx; the workload stands in for an ingress.
Tomcat, Windows, F5 and Citrix are still refused for ML-DSA.
records.note: During a Kubernetes rollback the workload can serve the new certificate for up to one kubelet sync period before the old one returns.

records.title: Ticket plugins: Zendesk, Freshservice
records.environment: Go test run in one process on SQLite. The real wasm of each plugin spoke https to a local service that keeps tickets in memory and can delete one behind the hub's back.
records.what_ran: Test connection, create, reconcile, recreate after an external delete, resolve, an outage, a refused credential, and audit rows, for both plugins.
not_proven: A real Zendesk account or Freshservice domain: plan limits, required fields, soft-delete responses, rate limits.
A ticket created just before a hub crash is not adopted on retry. This is a design limit.

evidence.label: Verdict line
evidence.text: ## Verdict: PASS against local stand-in services; no real Zendesk account or Freshservice domain was used

evidence.label: Results table
evidence.text:
| Step | Zendesk | Freshservice |
|---|---|---|
| Test connection: read-only `ticket.exists` for key `0`, "no such ticket" is OK | PASS | PASS |
| Create: event submitted, drained, row `created` with a key and an https link; the stand-in holds one open ticket | PASS | PASS |
| Exists: reconcile of a live ticket changes nothing (not recreated) | PASS | PASS |
| Externally deleted: reconcile recreates the ticket once, row flagged `recreated`, new key at the service | PASS | PASS |
| Resolve: `ResolveByFingerprint` closes the recreated ticket (Zendesk `solved`, Freshservice status 4), row `resolved` | PASS | PASS |
| Outage (stand-in answers 500): row stays `pending`, attempts 1, error classed temporary | PASS | PASS |
| Refused credential (401): row `failed`, error classed permanent; test connection returns a permanent error | PASS | PASS |
| Audit: native `itsm.ticket.create` success x2 and `itsm.ticket.resolve` x1; `delivery_plugin.ticket` rows carry kind, version and sha256 | PASS | PASS |
| No credential value (API token, API key) in any row error, alert or audit summary | PASS | PASS |

A run through a public CA such as Let's Encrypt staging.

records.title: 100,000-certificate benchmark
records.environment: Apple M4 Max, 64 GiB, macOS, Go 1.27.1, PostgreSQL 16 on the same machine. Hosted nightly runs on GitHub ubuntu-latest, 4 vCPU.
records.what_ran: Search, list and issue load against a hub holding 100,000 certificates, before and after a refresh fix and a memory-limit change.
records.counts: search p99 101 to 130 ms (bar under 500); peak RSS about 1.8 GiB (bar under 2 GiB)
not_proven: The 1,000,000-certificate run is still pending.
The last hosted nightly (before the harness fix) failed the memory bar; the next nightly is the check.
Issue rate varies 508 to 1690 requests a second on a shared machine, so that bar rests on a median of three passes.
RSS margin is about 200 MiB; larger estates need a redesign that is not done.
records.note: The first run missed the search and memory bars. A refresh fix brought search p99 from about 970 ms to about 110 ms.
